findings.problem: The explanations for 'law' and 'house' give a reason and a link that Acts 13:43 doesn't state. 'law' says Paul 'just finished saying the law of Moses couldn't justify them... So he points them somewhere better', which makes Acts 13:39 the reason for the urging in Acts 13:43. 'house' calls the grace 'God's grace that they just heard about through Jesus (Acts 13:38-39)', but the sermon never uses the word grace. The 'grace' explanation does the same thing in a smaller way: 'keep standing right there in that grace' points back to the forgiveness in Acts 13:38. The text says only that Paul and Barnabas urged them to continue in the grace of God.

rule.text: Reasons. He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The 'Continue this message on the next Sabbath' explanation puts quotation marks around a paraphrase of what the people said: the crowd says, “Do it again next week.” That is not the BSB wording of Acts 13:42. It is presented as a retelling of the people's words, not as Papa Dorin's own made-up joke line.

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: The 'Iconium' explanation repeats the oven-to-cookie-box gag, 'I get winded going from my oven to my cookie box.' Stop 1 card 3 (Prep) already used it word for word, and stop 1 card 2 'Home to Tarsus' has a version of it ('I once got lost walking from my oven to my cookie box'). Using the same joke in two explanations makes them sound alike.

rule.text: There is no formula. Each explanation sounds natural and different from the others.

findings.problem: The 'True' explanation opens with “Yes sir!”, which can read as calling the baker 'sir' and assumes their gender.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The 'Scoffers' explanation says “God says He's doing a work in their days.” Acts 13:40-41 only says the words were 'spoken by the prophets' and never names the speaker of the 'I'. The speaker is the LORD in Habakkuk 1:5, but that verse is outside the passage and isn't referenced. The 'Idol makers' and 'False shepherds' explanations also call it 'God's work'.
findings.question: When a passage quotes the prophets without naming who speaks, may Papa Dorin name God as the speaker using the source verse (here Hab 1:5)? If so, must he give that reference, or must he leave the speaker open the way Acts does?

findings.problem: The explanations call untying sandals 'the lowest job there is' ('sandals') and 'about the humblest job around' ('robe'). Acts 13:25 gives no such fact. It is cultural background with no reference behind it.
findings.question: In answer explanations, may Papa Dorin add cultural background that isn't in the passage (like untying sandals being a servant's lowest task) without a reference? Or does that count as stretching the text?
